structured_output.analysis: I read budget_bits 84617/26880 as an average of about 3.148 bits per weight. iso_3.15 already uses all of it (avg_bits 3.147953869047619), so any upgrade has to be paid for with a downgrade of the same size. The knapsack already picks the cheapest method per layer for the single-layer KL table. Every listed loss layer's next step up is bf16, which costs about 12.9 bits per weight. Moving to int4 helps (layer 27 up_proj: gptq_int3 0.0057 to gptq_int4 0.0022), but no int4 layer I can see in the records could be downgraded to pay for it. Measured whole-recipe KL is 0.436 against a prediction of 0.398, so the layers interact. Changing GPTQ options other than group size should not add stored bits. Every recipe so far used default options (act_order=false, damp=0.01), and 141 of the 196 layers are GPTQ-family int2 or int3, where act_order usually matters most. I propose option-only grids that keep the same per-layer methods and stay within budget.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Same methods as iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e), which used default options. This turns on act_order=true for all GPTQ-family layers, which should not add stored bits. The loss sits in 2- and 3-bit GPTQ MLP layers, e.g. layer 14 down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065) and layer 27 up_proj gptq_int3 0.0057 (Ef04d8aa7bded).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e) with act_order=true and damp=0.05. Some activations are heavy-tailed, e.g. layer 27 up_proj input kurtosis 1090 (E24beed188b6a), which suggests the Hessian may be ill-conditioned. Stronger damping may make the 2- and 3-bit fits more stable without adding bits.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp05
proposals.rationale: Control for the damping effect alone: iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e) with damp=0.05 and act_order left at its default. The concentrated loss is in rht_gptq_int2/int3 MLP layers, e.g. layer 18 gate_proj 0.00497 (Eb1dd74cd6447).
